channel.title: Palm Coast Observer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Palm Coast Observer (observerlocalnews.com)

item.title: Art to fill a need: Seabreeze students make bowls for 18th annual Empty Bowls fundraiser
item.description: Halifax Urban Ministries' fundraiser will be held on March 14, at the Ocean Center.

item.title: Daytona Police chief says traffic stop involving mayor's wife was not racially motivated
item.description: Chief Young said the stop was a part of increased enforcement patrols in the area. 'There is a saying in law enforcement that we are damned if we do and we're damned if we don't,' Young said.

item.title: Pedestrian killed in Valentine's Day crash on Ormond's South Orchard Street
item.description: The crash was caused after a 79-year-old driver ran a stop sign, Ormond Beach Police report.

item.title: Insight Chiropractic to celebrate grand opening in Ormond Beach
item.description: Also: Stretch Zone to host grand reopening, members reappointed to Halifax Health Board, new restaurants coming to One Daytona and more.

item.title: Multi-agency investigation ends regional burglary spree
item.description: Palm Coast man arrested in the act after coordinated surveillance across Flagler and Volusia counties

item.title: Eight decades of artistic freedom: Ormond Memorial Art Museum is celebrating 80 years of art, community and honoring veterans
item.description: This year marks a major anniversary for the museum, which got its start in 1946 after painter and WWI veteran Malcom Fraser began searching for a home for his life's works.

item.title: 'We have done everything we could': Palm Coast to recoup $2.3 million in splash pad settlement
item.description: The settlement ends a four-year lawsuit between the city and contractors who initially began work on the splash pad in 2018.

item.title: Hammock's future Modern Mexx restaurant to be moved to northeast corner of lot
item.description: Modern Mexx will replace the Fusion 386 restaurant on S.R. A1A. Flagler Planning Board member Thomas Connor said that though the setbacks do not meet LDC requirements, they are still an improvement.

item.title: Flagler County, Flagler Beach work to avoid lawsuit over Summertown
item.description: Four of five dispute issues resolved as officials work to protect floodplain land and prevent court action

item.title: ICI Homes' Palm Coast development to be donated for local essential workers
item.description: The Palm Coast City Council approved an application to increase the E Section development to 71 homes from 58, contingent on the property going toward affordable, quality homes for essential workers.
